note: After Emerson & Banks's description of the new species of 1965 (in English); soldier only, the measurement table of 6 specimens transcribed as given. The original spells the species pelliceus (misprinted peiliceus in a few places). The alate and the worker are not described in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Head dark and densely hairy, unique among the known species of the genus. The body size overlaps that of L. labralis, but the position of the fontanelle tube and the process of the fore coxa place it close to L. longilabius and L. brevilabius; the latter two are smaller.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Anterior half of the head and the postmentum dark brown, the posterior half of the head and the underside of the head paler reddish brown; the end of the fontanelle tube yellowish white; postclypeus about as dark as the front of the head, paler at the anterior margin; labrum pale reddish brown, with a white transparent labral rim at the end; antennae pale yellowish brown; mandibles dark brown over their whole length; pronotum and legs pale brown; abdominal tergites and sternites pale yellow and transparent. Head, clypeus, labrum and the anterior half of the postmentum densely hairy, the posterior half of the postmentum with a few short hairs; the end of the fontanelle tube with many hairs; the end of the labrum without hairs; the base of the mandibles with many hairs; anterior margin of the pronotum with short hairs, the middle and the lateral margins with many hairs and setae; coxae and legs with many setae and hairs; abdominal tergites and sternites abundantly hairy, with hairs of different lengths. Head suboval, narrowed in front, the sides and posterior margin convex, the posterior corners broadly rounded; fontanelle tube short and wide, its anterior margin level with the line between the antennal bases. Postmentum long, constricted near the posterior end, more than twice as long as its maximum width, the maximum width about 1.3 times the minimum width. Antennae 15-segmented, segments 3, 4 and 5 about equal in length and all shorter than segment 6. Labrum proportionally large. Apex of the mandibles moderately curved; the right mandible with a shallow concavity about 2/5 of the way from the condyle, immediately followed by a small tooth; the left mandible with a very small V-shaped concavity about 2/3 of the way from the condyle and a small triangular tooth about 1/3 of the way from the condyle. Anterior lobe of the pronotum large and concave, the posterior margin undulate, in lateral view the anterior lobe and the base forming an angle of about 150°—160°. The outer margin of the fore coxa with a distinct but small rounded process near its base. Measurements (holotype/range of 6 paratypes, mm): head length (to the apex of the mandibles) 4.33/4.27—4.39, head length (to the apex of the labrum) 3.78/3.47—3.85, head length (to the mandibular base) 3.05/2.85—3.14, head width 2.53/2.37—2.53, head thickness 2.06/1.86—2.06, fontanelle tube length 0.18/0.15—0.18, diameter of the end of the fontanelle tube 0.37/0.35—0.38, postmentum length 1.59/1.27—1.59, postmentum maximum width 0.74/0.68—0.74, postmentum minimum width 0.55/0.47—0.55, labrum length (middle) 0.71, (from the lateral base) 0.83, labrum width 0.76/0.73—0.76, left mandible length 1.53/1.51—1.63, pronotum length 0.77/0.76—0.87, width 1.44/1.39—1.51, hind tibia 1.97/1.94—2.08.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The type locality is Itabu Creek, a tributary of the upper New River, Akarai Mountains, British Guiana (1°42′N, 57°55′W); the holotype and paratypes are 6 soldiers together with workers, collected by E. R. Blake in October 1938 (month 10). The original describes the soldier only; neither the alate nor the worker is described.
